content:
Doc intent
- This is the first full macro baseline run for the Q1 2026 workload suite. It is not yet the locked baseline artifact; it’s the first pass to (a) validate harness repeatability, (b) surface variance sources, and (c) identify runtime/kernel/scheduler hotspots before we freeze baselines.
- Audience: Runtime (kernels/scheduling), SRE (variance), Release Eng (gate design), Product (what’s publishable later).

Run metadata
- Run name: q1-2026-baseline-run-1
- Run window (UTC): 2026-02-11 19:10 → 2026-02-12 05:40
- Runner: benchmark-lab@v0.8.3 (runner schema v2)
- Workload suite: workload-suite-v0-draft (Drive: shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/workload-suite-v0-draft)
- Traffic shapes revision: ts-taxonomy-r3 (matches Confluence “representative-traffic-shapes-taxonomy” draft)
- Runtime build: redwood inference runtime commit 6c3a9d17 (built from release/2026.02.10-rc2)
- Scheduler config: sched_profile=prod_default; fairness=v2; load_shed=disabled
- Kernel selection: autotune=on (NOTE: nondeterminism risk; see ENG-4829)
- Regions: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-central-1
- Hardware pools used:
  - NVIDIA H100-SXM 80GB (driver 550.54.14; CUDA 12.4; NCCL 2.20.5)
  - NVIDIA A100-SXM4 80GB (driver 550.54.14; CUDA 12.4; NCCL 2.20.5)
- Fleet note: eu-central-1 had ~18% nodes on driver 550.40.* during first trial block (see “Known issues / annotations”).

Metric definitions (quick)
- TTFT: time-to-first-token (ms). For streaming, measured server-side at first chunk flush timestamp.
- TPOT: time-per-output-token during steady-state decode (ms/token), excluding TTFT.
- E2E latency: for non-streaming only; includes queue + prefill + decode until final token (ms).
- Throughput: tokens/s at the server (aggregate over successful requests; excludes retries).
- Error rate: HTTP non-2xx + runtime aborts.

Variance budget (from methodology draft; applied as “soft” for Run 1)
- Pass criteria (informational only for Run 1):
  - TTFT p95: ±5% max deviation across trials (same model/shape/region/hw)
  - TPOT p95: ±3%
  - Throughput p95: ±4%
  - p99 tail metrics may exceed budget in bursty shapes; must be explainable with scheduler metrics (queue wait, backpressure, batch composition).

How to read the table
- Each row = (model x quant profile x context x traffic shape x region x hardware).
- “Trials” = number of repeated runs used for variance stats (each trial is 15 min steady-state after warmup).
- “Var notes” includes whether we stayed within the above budgets and suspected causes when not.

Top-line summary (Run 1)
- Repeatability: H100 in us-east-1/us-west-2 was within budget for most shapes for both TTFT and TPOT. A100 showed higher p99 spread under bursty concurrency due to queueing sensitivity.
- Anomaly: Long-context streaming shape (TS-3) showed TTFT p99 regression + higher variance in eu-central-1 only; root cause likely fleet driver mismatch + first-chunk timestamp edge case (see redwood PR-23944).
- Scheduler: Under bursty concurrency (TS-4), p99 E2E and TTFT are strongly correlated with queue wait histograms; we need to ensure scheduler metrics required by “scheduler-metrics-required-for-baselines” are present in runner output for explainability.

Results table (macro benchmarks)

- Model: canonical name
- Quant: fp16 | int8
- Ctx: max context evaluated for this row
- Shape: TS-* shorthand
- Streaming: yes/no
- Conc: target concurrency (steady-state unless noted)
- Prompt/Out: target token ranges (P50/P95)
- Region / HW: execution location
- Trials: N
- Success%: successful requests / total
- TTFT (ms): p50 / p95 / p99
- TPOT (ms/tok): p50 / p95 / p99
- E2E (ms): p50 / p95 / p99 (non-streaming only)
- Throughput (tok/s): p50 / p95
- Var notes: within/outside variance budget and any notes

Traffic shapes used in this sheet
- TS-1: Chat short prompts, short outputs, streaming ("support-agent")
  - Prompt tokens: P50~220 / P95~650
  - Output tokens: P50~180 / P95~420
  - Concurrency: 32 steady
  - Cache: warm prefix cache enabled; expected hit ~35%
- TS-2: Chat short prompts, non-streaming ("api-batch-ish")
  - Prompt tokens: P50~180 / P95~500
  - Output tokens: P50~240 / P95~600
  - Concurrency: 16 steady
  - Cache: warm; expected hit ~25%
- TS-3: Long-context chat, streaming ("devtools long ctx")
  - Prompt tokens: P50~4.5k / P95~12k
  - Output tokens: P50~280 / P95~800
  - Concurrency: 8 steady
  - Cache: cold→warm ramp (0%→15%); expected hit ~8% at steady
- TS-4: Bursty concurrency ramp, streaming ("burst + mixed tenants")
  - Prompt tokens: P50~300 / P95~1.2k
  - Output tokens: P50~220 / P95~650
  - Concurrency: ramp 8→64 every 3 min; hold 64 for 6 min; repeat
  - Cache: warm; expected hit ~30%; backpressure expected

Known issues / annotations
1) eu-central-1 driver mix
- Observed: non-uniform driver versions across benchmark pool for first block (about 18% nodes on 550.40.*).
- Impact: TTFT p99 tails inflated and higher inter-trial variance (esp TS-1 and TS-3).
- Tracking: Jira INT-1440. Action: enforce driver/CUDA pinning at runner scheduler layer; rerun eu-central-1 after remediation.

2) Streaming TTFT timestamp edge case
- Observed: In TS-3, some runs showed TTFT p99 spikes without corresponding queue wait spikes.
- Hypothesis: first-chunk flush timestamp misrecorded when chunking/flush cadence interacts with first token emission under long prefill.
- Fix: redwood PR-23944 (not included in Run 1). Action: rerun TS-3 on H100 post-merge and compare server-side TTFT vs client-measured TTFT (ENG-4832).

3) Autotune nondeterminism
- Observed: small but non-zero TPOT jitter across trials on A100, and occasional TTFT shifts on long prefill.
- Action: proceed with ENG-4829 (pinning/seed handling, reduce autotune jitter for baseline-critical kernels). For locked baselines, we likely need autotune either (a) disabled for critical kernels or (b) precomputed + cached deterministically.
